_notes: consumer 'alerts' is in authorized_consumers of .es-query on Serverless 9.6 (alongside stackAlerts, discover, logs, observability, infrastructure); source: GET /api/alerting/rule_types. 'stackAlerts' is the alternative for Stack-style rules.
action group 'query matched' confirmed from the same listing.

Interim results are EXCLUDED (is_interim=false) so an alert only fires on finalized bucket results and cannot fire on a value that later disappears. Trade-off: the alert is delayed until the 15m bucket is finalized (up to bucket_span + query_delay after the bucket starts). The native rule mlws-ml-native-record also uses includeInterim=false, so the two are comparable.

The 'timestamp' of an ML record is the START of its bucket, so with a 30m window a record is only found while bucket start is within the last 30m. A 30m window on 15m buckets can miss a record that is finalized late; this is the point of the 15m vs 30m comparison.

groupBy=top over termField [job_id, partition_field_value] gives one alert per (job, partition) (service, app_code, site); multi-field grouping is supported for 2-4 fields. Records without a partition (e.g. population jobs) are not grouped. Reading .ml-anomalies-* from a rule on Serverless needs the rule API key to have read on .ml-anomalies-* (confirm in an end-to-end run).
The esQuery filter is scoped to the single job mlws-apm-multimetric (term job_id). A prefix filter (prefix job_id) would cover every job in one rule; here one job keeps the workshop alert readable.

Mustache cannot compute a max over hits, so the alert payload carries a 'records' list with one entry per hit (job, partition, score, actual, typical, function, field, timestamp, influencers, explorer link); hit_count is context.value (number of matching records).

params.subject: [ML Workshop] ML per-partition (30m look-back): {{alert.id}} ({{context.value}} records)
